title: Part Three, Chapter 6: The Departure from Tulanzú

verses.t: And another tribe or branch stole the fire in the smoke; these were the people of the house of bats, and their god was called Chamalcan, of the Cakchiquels, and he was in the likeness of a bat when he passed through the smoke; and passing softly, he came and took fire. And the Cakchiquels did not ask for the fire, and would not let themselves be overcome; only the peoples who gave their side and their tobacco to be opened were overcome. And this was what the god had spoken of, when the whole people was sacrificed before him, and their hearts were torn out through the side and the tobacco; and it had not yet begun to be done when this was told them in this figure by Tohil, and death in majesty, through Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam. And from there, from Tulanzú, came this custom of not eating but fasting always, and only waiting for the dawn and to see the face of the sun. And they took turns watching that great star called the morning star, which is the one that goes before when the sun comes out, the beautiful morning star that was always there in the East when they were there in Tulanzú; for this was the name of the place the god came from. And it was not here that they received the greatness of their kingdom; rather, there all the peoples, small and great, were subdued, when they sacrificed before Tohil and all the men gave the blood of their side and their tobacco. And in an instant there came from there their greatness and the great knowledge they had in the darkness of the night, when they did all this. And they came away and tore themselves from there, and left the East. "This is not our homeland," said Tohil. "Let us go and see where we are to settle!" For truly Tohil spoke to Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam: "Come, give thanks first: pierce the tips of your ears and pass something through them, and your elbows too, and this will be your thanksgiving before the god." "Very well," they said, and then they pierced their ears; and they put it into their song of the coming from Tulanzú, and their hearts wept when they came away and left Tulanzú: "Here we shall not see the rising of the sun, which brightens the face of the earth!" they said as they came. And they left people on the road, and truly some stayed sleeping in each of the towns; they rose up, for they were continually watching the star, the sign of the sun. And this was the sign they believed was of the dawn when they came from the East; and their faces were all alike when they came from there; and there was a great distance, so it is told us now.
